native_mechanisms: A rolling sphere serves as the sole carried memory across the whole ordered pile (single running accumulator, no per-position state or lookback).
A fixed count of tumbles down a mason trail mixes each mark into the sphere before the next is taken (fixed number of shift/strike mixing steps per input byte, avalanching the whole accumulator).

Only the final hairline crack in the last stalk is kept as the token, while all intermediate cracks and dust are swept away (a final finishing mix on the accumulator yields the output; intermediates discarded).
core_technique: Bob Jenkins one-at-a-time hash widened to 64 bits: per-byte add plus a fixed add-shift/xor-shift mixing pair on a single accumulator, followed by a three-step shift/xor/add finalizer — no multiplication, so not FNV/xxHash multiply-based mixing.
